thesis: TMO sits within 0.9% of its 52-week high after a run of sell-side price-target hikes (UBS to $730 on 9/9, Baird to $686 on 9/3, HSBC to $690 on 9/1) and a July beat-and-raise Q2 print, but today's push higher coincided with a broad life-sciences-tools sector rally at the Morgan Stanley Healthcare Conference (RVTY, DGX, ILMN, CAI all up alongside TMO) rather than a fresh TMO-specific catalyst. invalidation: The life-sciences-tools group gives back this rally, or a subsequent print misses the mid-single-digit 2027 organic growth UBS is modeling.

thesis: CNQ is up roughly 17.4% over the trailing 60 days and sits just 1.5% below its 52-week high, supported by a genuine Q2 beat (adjusted EPS ~C$2.15-2.19 vs. ~C$2.01 est., revenue C$14.74B vs. C$13.36B est., reported 8/6) and a subsequent CIBC price-target raise (8/27, to C$75). Even so, a large share of this 60-day move tracks the broader oil-price shock from the Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz conflict that lifted the entire E&P sector (WTI moved from the high-$70s to above $100 in September) rather than a CNQ-specific re-rating -- so despite the earnings beat, the size of the move is largely a commodity/macro effect, keeping this a lower-conviction long. Nothing surfaced this run on active litigation, dilution, insolvency/liquidity concerns, or leadership turnover.
invalidation: WTI crude gives back the geopolitical risk premium and CNQ's price move reverses without any change in company fundamentals, or Q3 results miss versus raised expectations.

thesis: ASML fell about 6% on 9/14 and remains pressured, but the decline tracks a sector-wide, sentiment-driven selloff across semiconductor-equipment names after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call for the AI industry to slow model-capability development, which also hit SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron, Nvidia and Intel -- not a company-specific deterioration at ASML. ASML's own fundamentals remain intact: a Q2 beat-and-raise (EPS $8.82 vs. $7.98 est., FY26 sales guidance raised to EUR43-45B), JPMorgan reporting 2027 EUV capacity is nearly sold out with 2028 machine demand already being booked, and continued expansion (Samsung High-NA EUV partnership, new Netherlands campus). No active litigation, dilution, insolvency/liquidity concern, or leadership turnover surfaced this run.
invalidation: AI-capex spending actually slows in a way that shows up in ASML's order book or 2027/2028 EUV bookings, rather than remaining a sentiment-only reaction.
